intent: To demonstrate the historical trend of increasing democratic governance from autocracy between 1900 and 2000.

units.meaning: Democracy share starts low at 14.7% in 1900 and ends high at 97.1% in 2000, showing the century-long shift from low to high democratic governance.
accepted_routes: Democracy share rises from 14.7% in 1900 to 97.1% in 2000.
The series starts near 15% and ends near 97%.
By 2000, democracy share reaches 97.1%, up from 14.7% at the start of the century.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must show the line or area at 1900 near 14.7% and at 2000 near 97.1%, with visible overall upward trajectory.
units.temporal_anchor: opening/closing narration around 'from autocracy' and 'to democracy'.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video state both 1900 and 2000 endpoint values, or is showing the overall upward trend sufficient?

units.meaning: The net century-long increase in democracy share is 82.4 percentage points.
accepted_routes: Democracy share increases by 82.4 percentage points over the century.
Net change equals +82.4 percentage points from 14.7% to 97.1%.
units.visual_evidence_rule: A visible annotation or vertical difference between the start and end values must support the +82.4 percentage-point gain.
units.reviewer_question: Is the net +82.4 percentage-point increase required, or is it optional detail?

units.meaning: Democracy share crosses the 50% majority threshold around 1970, first exceeding half at 50.2% after being 48.7% in 1968.

basis.note: last shown value below 50% before crossing

accepted_routes: Democracy share crosses the 50% line in 1970, reaching 50.2%.
It is still below half in 1968 at 48.7% and first exceeds half in 1970 at 50.2%.
The series passes the majority threshold between 1968 and 1970.
By 1970, democracy share is just over half.
units.visual_evidence_rule: A 50% horizontal reference line must be visible, with the series crossing it between 1968 and 1970.
units.temporal_anchor: mid-clip narration around the transition to democracy, before the late-century rise.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly mark the 50% majority threshold crossing, or can it omit that milestone?

units.meaning: The 1980s show a steep late-century acceleration: democracy share rises from 55.2% in 1980 to 88.8% in 1990, a gain of 33.6 percentage points.
accepted_routes: Between 1980 and 1990, democracy share jumps from 55.2% to 88.8%, adding 33.6 percentage points.
The 1980s show a steep acceleration from just over 55% to nearly 89%.
A rapid late-century climb adds 33.6 percentage points in the 1980-1990 interval.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must show a visibly steeper slope or expanded area between 1980 and 1990, with those years labeled or traceable.
units.temporal_anchor: late-clip narration if it emphasizes rapid development after 1980.
units.reviewer_question: Should the 1980s acceleration be included as essential, or is it optional context?

units.meaning: The long-term rise is not monotonic: democracy share falls from a local 1924 peak of 28.3% to 13.2% by 1936, a drop of 15.1 percentage points.
accepted_routes: After rising early, democracy share falls from 28.3% in 1924 to 13.2% in 1936.
The trend is not monotonic: it loses 15.1 percentage points between 1924 and 1936.
A visible early reversal interrupts the long-term upward trend.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must show a local peak around 1924 and a trough around 1936, making the reversal visible.
units.temporal_anchor: early/mid-clip narration if it acknowledges setbacks or non-monotonic history.
units.reviewer_question: Should the video show the 1924-1936 reversal, or may it present only the net upward trend?

optional_valid: Democracy share is flat at 14.7% from 1900 through 1908.
Democracy share first reaches 40% in 1954 at 40.8%.
By 1996 democracy share reaches 94.1%, and by 2000 it reaches 97.1%.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claims that specific wars, institutions, or events caused democratic expansion.
Extrapolating beyond 2000 or claiming democracy share will reach 100%.
Calling the trend perfectly steady or monotonic despite the 1924-1936 decline.
Using an unstated denominator such as countries or population unless the table explicitly supports it.
Stating autocracy share values unless explicitly computed as 100 - democracy share and labeled as derived.
notes: The table contains one estimated series, democracy share, so all numeric claims must be temporal or arithmetic from that series. U3-U5 are the main trade-offs: the 50% threshold, the 1980s acceleration, and the interwar reversal.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
